_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
12/13 2:53PM - Now that's how you weekend! The stoke here goes beyond the summit and we’re ready to keep the energy rolling into Sunday. Tomorrow, we plan on having 74 ways down, 50 of which are scheduled for some quality time with the groomers. You’ll find 11 ways up with no anticipated delays. Just in case you missed out on the In a Pickle Rail Jam, our parks team has decided to open up the rails to the public tomorrow! Rest up and check back bright and early for your morning report. Let’s Weekend!

The Sun Bowl is now open for lift, lodge and parking access! Sunrise Express will be open and spinning at 8:30AM - there is no early access available at Sunrise this weekend. PLEASE NOTE: Sun Bowl’s terrain is for expert skiers and riders only, with natural snow coverage, ungroomed conditions and unmarked hazards. All beginner skiers and Riders should stick to the main face of the mountain. Along with that, snowmaking is set to resume shortly with the goal to open Black Bear as soon as possible from the top, Big Ben, tubing, and more Sun Bowl trails. 

Safety Tip: Look uphill and yield while merging.

Ice Skating is now open! Lace up and head to the Mill House skating pond for a day or night of winter fun. Enjoy music and a campfire all while gliding under the stars. Book now to guarantee your place on the ice.

Guided Snowmobile Tours are back! Explore Stratton after hours with friends and family on a tour to the summit. Be sure to book your spot now to guarantee your spot.

The Nordic Center is now open for Nordic Skiing and Snowshoeing! Enjoy the peaceful 10km of trails with friends or family.  

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: Break out your sunglasses for a warm and sunny Saturday — if the sun is out we’re having fun! Expect crispy snow to start the day followed by softer snow as temperatures warm into the low 40s. Icy sections are present in heavily compacted and shady areas. Now is the time to sharpen your edges and bust out the skinny skis. Check your speed and keep an eye out for other skiers and riders, especially at merge zones and breakovers. Moonbeam Express, Apex Express, Link, and the Magic Carpet are open, providing access to 7 trails and the Upper Tude Dudes Terrain Park. Due to early-season conditions, we currently have no beginner terrain accessible from Moonbeam. 12 Days of Holiday Cheer is now underway, with daily holiday events through Christmas. Drop into Solitude Village to browse the holiday market both days this weekend.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is Laurie with your 5 am snow report for Saturday, December 13th. Remember the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website.  
Our Mid mountain base is 16 inches, the temperature is 34 degrees, the winds are 11 miles per hour from the SW, with clear skies. 
The Summit base is 21 inches, the temperature is 22 degrees, the winds are 20 miles per hour from the WNW, with clear skies. 
The base temperature is 14 degrees.  
We will be skiing and riding on 11 lifts, 23 runs, and 169 acres on PP/MM snow.  
It’s a big Saturday in Steamboat as the Visa Big Air World Cup Finals take center stage, with live music from The Motet, a U.S. Ski & Snowboard athlete autograph session, and a hot air balloon glow at sunset. Timber & Torch and The Range will be open throughout the evening. It’s a full day of excitement, you won't want to miss. Visit steamboat.com/events for full details.  
Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more.  
If you are thinking of exploring outside the ski area boundaries, and don’t know exactly where you are going, don’t go.  
Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
12/11 Operations Update: Hello Crystal skiers and riders, the mountain will remain closed  through Tuesday 12/16 with opening day still TBA. Stay tuned for updates towards early next week.

Please refer to WSDOT and the Enumclaw Police Dept page for any updates on the status of highway 410. We encourage everyone to avoid any travel on 410 for now due to risk of treefall and mudslides. A huge shout out to the Crystal and Greenwater community who’ve been working hard, out filling sandbags, firing up generators, and helping neighbors along the 410 corridor these last couple days. 

Near record-breaking rainfall and warm temperatures across Western Washington this week have not provided any relief to our low snowpack, but the forecast shows a return to cold temperatures and the potential for much needed snowfall Tuesday and onwards. We are hopeful about this pattern shift. Looking back, the 08/09 winter season was also a La Niña Year and we didn't open until December 13, but still received above average snowfall at 463" throughout the season. Mountain operations teams remain at the ready as soon as the required conditions are there, and we can all start doing what we do best! Until then, stay safe, stay dry, and keep thinking SNOW. 

  • Webcams (other than the ridgeline panocam) are offline due to a mountain power outage.
  • Season to date snowfall + Base Depths reported as of  12/11. Overnight and 24 hour totals will be updated regularly upon season start. 
  • Parking reservations for days we are closed will be automatically canceled with no penalties, and any payments will be refunded.
  • Day tickets and rentals purchased in advance on days we are closed can be deferred to a different day with applicable price adjustments by emailing gservice@skicrystal.com or giving us a call daily from 9:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. at 833-279-7895, or will otherwise be automatically refunded after 2pm before the day of your booking. 
  • For Ski and Ride School + Freeride programs and single days, keep an eye out for further communications through email on re-bookings and refunds.

ADVANCED PARKING RESERVATIONS FOR THE SEASON ARE OPEN. BOOK YOURS HERE.
Shuttle Reservations on are open for 7 day window bookings. Reminder-  reservation cancellations are now required this year.

PRE-SEASON UPHILL TRAVEL INFO: Uphill travel may be restricted at any time before and during the season for avalanche mitigation or other safety concerns. Uphill travelers must confirm that the "No Uphill Travel lights" are off. These are located at: The bottom station of the Gondola, Bottom lift shack of Discovery lift the bottom lift shack of Chinook Express lift and the top of Quicksilver.
  • Slopes are not avalanche-controlled. Ski and ride at your own risk.
  • Be aware of heavy equipment across the mountain. Be sure you are visible and give ample space to moving vehicles.
  • In case of incident, Ski Patrol may not be available to help. Rescue, if possible, will be delayed and may cost you. Come prepared and self-sufficient.
 An Uphill Travel pass is required during the regular season and can be obtained at no cost at Guest Services. For complete information see our Uphill Travel Page.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
December 13th, 1:25 PM
Good afternoon, Sugarbush skiers and riders! Snow is coming down, and vibes are going up! Castlerock and Valley House lifts made their season debut at 9:00 AM, and North Lynx terrain is open for hiking only from 10:00 AM - 3:00 PM. Tomorrow's a cold one, expect cloudy skies with base temps in the teens, summit temps in the single digits, and chance of snow showers throughout the day. Please note: Castlerock runout is very thin and may damage equipment, choose wisely.

We'll be getting down on 66 trails, 6 lifts, and 280 skiable acres, including plenty of natural terrain off Castlerock and North Lynx, suggested for experts only. Natural terrain conditions are thin and variable, so assess before riding and use caution. Packed powder and top-tier corduroy are waiting for you on 19 trails. Hunt the edges for the best turns, wind has pushed fresh snow off the center, leaving stashes along the sides. Snowmaking has wrapped up on mid-mountain trails Downspout, Lower Downspout, and Lower Jester. Groomers will be over them tonight, flattening whales to a skiable surface.

Super Bravo and Heaven’s Gate begin loading at 8:00 AM, all other lifts at 9:00 AM. Reminder terrain off upper mountain lifts is for advanced skiers and riders only. Mt. Ellen hike park is open with 20 freestyle features from 10:00 AM–3:00 PM for passholders, plus, tomorrow Slowpoke will be home to 3 new freestyle features. Both Lincoln Peak Morning and Evening Routes are open for Uphill Travel, check our policy for details. We're getting close! Mt. Ellen opening day is officially less than a week away!

Join us tonight at 6:00 PM at Gate House Lodge for our Wall of Fame celebration, followed by live music at 7:00 PM from The Talking Dreads during Sugarbash. Bust out your boldest, or ugliest, holiday sweater for our fan-favorite contest. Check out all of our winter events!

Have an Ikon Base Pass? Come ski before 12/25 and earn a voucher for an unrestricted lift ticket for yourself to be used any day here for the rest of the season. Grab up to five of these tickets simply by skiing and riding here before Christmas. Don't miss out on all of our deals including 50% off December lodging through December 26th.

Bonjour Tremblant!

Winter has been on fire these past few days!
This wonderful Saturday morning brings 10 cm of fresh snow, and conditions on the mountain are simply incredible. Today, the atmosphere is electric with 24H Tremblant in full swing!

Please note that some runs on the South Side are reserved for the 24h event. 

Whether you’re skiing, cheering on participants, or soaking up the festive atmosphere, everything is in place for a memorable day. Have fun and enjoy the full Tremblant experience!

Mountain safety tip of the week: At intersections, give way to those higher up! Give way to those higher up when entering a trail and at intersections. 

Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
